title: Device theft and tampering
goal_html: Pairs act as the IT security triage desk, reviewing a stack of device incident reports (thefts and tampering findings) and assigning each a risk level with a justification tied to encryption status, seal status, and detection delay. Ties to LO 2.2.B, 2.2.C and the course skill Analyze Risk.
reference_html:
Incident sheet (print or project)

steps_html:
1. (5 min) Each pair reads incidents 1-3 (theft reports) independently and writes their risk level and one-sentence justification for each.
  2. (5 min) Partners compare answers. Where they disagree, each must defend their call by citing the specific rule (encryption status, sensitivity, hours since check). Reach consensus.
  3. (5 min) Repeat for incidents 4-6 (tampering reports), paying attention to why incident 5 is riskier than incident 6 despite both having an intact seal.
  4. (5 min) Each pair opens the simulation and checks their triage decisions against the sim's scoring for equivalent scenarios; revise any incorrect calls and note which rule they misapplied.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "incident responder" (assigns the risk level and decides who to notify), the other is the "policy auditor" (checks whether the responder's justification actually matches the written rule rather than a gut feeling). For incident 5, the pair must specifically discuss why an intact seal is not sufficient evidence that no tampering occurred. Swap roles halfway through.
exit_html: Each student writes one sentence: "Incident X is [risk level] because [rule applied], and [control] would have reduced the risk by [mechanism]."
